::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Evaluate $ \int_{a}^{b}(A - f(x))dx$ where $A = [1/(b-a)] \cdot \int_a^b f(x)\,dx$](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1111366/evaluate-int-aba-fxdx-where-a-1-b-a-cdot-int-ab-fx-d), asked by [Fazel N](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/175176/fazel-n) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-01-20; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> My solution:
>
> Using the definition of the integral, rewrite $f(x)$ in the expression $A = [1/(b-a)] \cdot \int_a^b f(x) \, dx$ as:
>
> $$A = \frac1{b-a} \sum_{i = 0}^{n \to +\infty} f(x)\frac{b-a}n$$
>
> The $b-a$ terms then cancel each other out resulting in:
>
>
> $$A = \sum_{i = 0}^{n \to+\infty} \frac{f(x)}n$$ which is equal to $0$.
>
> Therefore, the original expression $\int_a^b (A - f(x)) \, dx$ simplifies to:
>
> $$-\int_a^b f(x) \, dx$$
>
> I'm not sure if I've approached the problem correctly, and if my final expression should be rewritten in a simpler form (if possible).
>
> Help or Confirmation?
:::

Hint:  What is
$$\int_a^b A\,dx$$

<!---
Full solution: 
$$\begin{align*}
    \int_a^b(A - f(x))\,dx &= \int_a^b A\,dx - \int_a^b f(x)\,dx \\
    &= A(b-a) - \int_a^b f(x)\,dx \\
    &= \int_a^b f(x)\,dx - \int_a^b f(x)\,dx \\
    &= 0
\end{align*}$$
-->
